cutset_contract.meaning: A selected cutset variable is deleted from the primal graph only as a structural probe. R24 does not assign it 0/1, enumerate its values, simplify clauses semantically, or execute a Boolean branch.
cutset_contract.eligible_vertices: remaining internal variables only; frozen R19 bridge variables are never selected
cutset_contract.greedy_lookahead_rule: At each round, for every eligible remaining internal variable v, delete v and its incident edges from the current primal graph; run both frozen R23 internal elimination heuristics on that reduced graph; score v lexicographically by (minimum induced width across MIN_FILL_INTERNAL and MIN_DEGREE_INTERNAL, maximum induced width across the two, minimum total fill edges across the two, negative current degree of v, negative original frame literal-occurrence count of v, numeric variable id ascending). Select the unique lexicographic minimum, permanently delete it for the next round, and never revise earlier choices.
cutset_contract.bridge_behavior: bridge vertices remain present as neighbors and are never eliminated by the width heuristics

measurements_per_profile_size: MIN_FILL_INTERNAL induced width and fill edges
MIN_DEGREE_INTERNAL induced width and fill edges

verdict_rules.small_cutset_promising: R24_SMALL_STRUCTURAL_CUTSET_PROMISING if minimum frozen heuristic width reaches <=20 at any k<=8.
verdict_rules.concentrated_core_signal: If small_cutset_promising is false, R24_CONCENTRATED_STRUCTURAL_CORE_SIGNAL if width drop from k=0 to k=8 is >=16.
verdict_rules.distributed_width_signal: If neither prior rule holds, R24_DISTRIBUTED_WIDTH_SIGNAL if width drop from k=0 to k=8 is <=8.
verdict_rules.mixed: All other integrity-valid outcomes are R24_MIXED_CUTSET_WIDTH_SIGNAL.

interpretation_limits: Deleting k graph vertices is a structural sensitivity probe, not a proof that a semantic algorithm can branch on 2^k assignments efficiently.
The resulting induced widths are upper bounds for the two frozen heuristic orders, not exact treewidth.
A large width drop may motivate a new symbolic separator representation, but cannot by itself authorize assignment enumeration inside a candidate.
next_action_rule: Only after R24 preserves the cutset-width profile may a new semantic representation be proposed. If width remains distributed, do not hide exponential cutset enumeration behind the word factorization.
claim_ceiling: Exposed graph-structural sensitivity on one frozen world only. No semantic verdict, no treewidth theorem, no polynomial scaling, no SAT-in-P, P=NP, or P!=NP conclusion.
